text:
eli: FYI staging p99 jumped after the v2.3.1 model onboard. Observed KV prefetch starving short sequences + kernel selector flipped to fallback kernel (coral fallback).
marta: saw it ~10:22, p99 went from ~120ms -> ~360ms on several routes. :eyes:
sajid: I grabbed a flamegraph and a perf trace. Looks like KV cache lock contention + tokenizer sync call holding the batch scheduler thread.
eli: Paste of the notable stack sample:
```
batch_scheduler:wait_for_batch -> tokenizer.sync_load -> kv.prefetch(blocking) -> kernel_selector(fallback)
# hot functions: kv::lock_wait, tokenizer::sync_load, batch::enqueue
```
build-bot: CI perf gate failed: e2e/perf_p99 exceeded threshold on the model-onboard job. Test log: `perf_p99: 372ms > limit 200ms`
ops-bot: Can we revert the onboard? If that removes the tokenizer sync change it might fix it.
marta: Bisect points at commit c7f9fa9 — "tokenizer: sync prefetch on first-batch to warm vocab". Repro locally with `prefetch.enabled=true` and many short tails.
sajid: Quick mitigation applied to staging overrides: set `kv.prefetch.concurrent=1` and `batch_scheduler.yield_ms=2`. Also disabled `tokenizer.sync_on_load`.
eli: Applying staging patch now and pausing canary. Will monitor p99.
revert-bot: Revert PR opened: r3456-revert-tokenizer-prefetch (CI triggered).
marta: Note root cause: when sequence-length distribution is heavy on short sequences, sync prefetch grabs KV lock, blocks scheduler, batches pile up and kernel selector sees pathological seq patterns and falls back. Two problems: blocking prefetch + sync tokenizer call.
sajid: Proposed follow-up: change prefetch to async per-worker and add a small backpressure window for sequences < 8 tokens. Filing issue #4412 and RFC doc link: https://redwood.internal/rfc/4412 (will attach perf traces).
eli: After the config tweak staging p99 ~130ms now. Keeping canary paused until revert merges and async-prefetch is implemented.
ops-bot: Notified on-call: @sajid @marta @eli.
marta: Quick note for postmortem: add unit/regression test to CI that simulates many short-tail requests and asserts no kernel selector fallback under normal prefetch config.
eli: Agreed — also schedule a kernel-selector test harness run for the model catalog change.
